title: Schedule of Enrollable Charges by Patient Payment Plan Tier
content:
For every tier of the Patient Payment Plan, this schedule states which kinds of patient charge may be taken into the plan and how old a charge may be. The age limit is the most calendar days that may lie between a charge's posting date and the date it is enrolled or added on.

## Schedule

| Tier | Missed-visit fees enrollable | Time-of-service deductible estimates enrollable before the payer has adjudicated the visit | Charges already transferred to collections enrollable | Charge-age limit (calendar days from posting date to enrollment or add-on date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short-Term 3-Month Payment Plan | No | No | No | 120 |
| Standard 6-Month Payment Plan | No | No | No | 120 |
| Extended 10-Month Payment Plan | No | No | No | 120 |
| Long-Term 12-Month Payment Plan | No | No | No | 120 |
| Large-Balance 18-Month Payment Plan | No | No | No | 120 |
| Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan | No | No | No | 365 |

## Notes to the schedule

1. The three exclusion columns read the same on every tier: no tier of the Patient Payment Plan enrolls missed-visit fees, deductible estimates awaiting adjudication, or charges already transferred to collections.
2. The charge-age limit is 120 calendar days on five tiers and 365 calendar days on the Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan.
3. Hypothetical comparison: a charge whose posting date lies 200 calendar days before the enrollment date is beyond the limit of 120 days but within the limit of 365 days.
